frozen_problem.title: A fixed-base descending sequence from Monsky quartics
frozen_problem.statement: Fix $d$. Does there exist a sequence of singular algebras $\{ R_n \}$ over a fixed finite field of characteristic $p>0$, and of dimension $d$, such that the $e_{HK}\left(R_n\right)$ descend to some number $\alpha_d$ from above?

theory.target: Test exact Frobenius-quotient length transport under the coefficient pullback A=F2+m inside B=F_(2^r)[x,y,z_1,...,z_(d-1)]/(xy), localized at the origin; determine whether forcing residue field F2 preserves Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity.
definitions: q=p^e, n^[q] is generated by all q-th powers from n, and L_R(q)=length_R(R/n^[q]).
B has coefficient/residue field K; A=k+m has residue k and is a different ring.
r=[K:k], d is the common positive Krull dimension.
The node family is the local ring of K[x,y,z_1,...,z_(d-1)]/(xy) at its origin.
Finite experiments use k=F2 and polynomial-basis K of degrees1..4.
assumptions: Characteristic2, finite perfect coefficient field K=F_(2^r), k=F2, r>=1.
B is the localization at the homogeneous maximal ideal of K[x,y,z_1,...,z_(d-1)]/(xy), with dimension d>=1 and residue field K.
A=k+m is a different local ring with residue k, not merely B viewed as a k-algebra.
Finite quotient computations use a coordinate cap q+1, which is above q; discarded higher monomials must already belong to the Frobenius ideal.
The universal length transport proof and Noetherian/local model identification require independent review. No Monsky quartic computation or parent solution is claimed.
approaches_considered: Prove K-stability of the Frobenius ideal using coefficient roots, then apply an A-module exact sequence and length restriction.
Count monomial normal forms on the two node branches, correcting their overlap and the constant coefficient.
Build a finite truncated pullback algebra and independently compute the F2-rank of all generator-product columns.
falsification_targets: Pullback to the fixed residue field preserves finite Frobenius quotient lengths.
Multiplying the old length by residue degree gives the exact answer without a constant correction.
The proposed basis omits a coefficient direction or includes a Frobenius-ideal vector.

claims.statement: The coefficient pullback preserves every finite Frobenius-quotient length. Refuted for K=F4,k=F2,B=(K[x,y]/xy)_(x,y),q=2: intrinsic lengths are3 for B and5 for A=k+m.
claims.falsification_condition: Wrong local-model identification, ideal generators, field arithmetic or quotient basis.

claims.statement: The exact finite length is r*L_B(q) without correction. Refuted in the same example: this predicts6 instead of5; q=1 also distinguishes residue length1 from r.
claims.falsification_condition: A wrong quotient basis or mistaken constant-coefficient field in A.

claims.statement: For finite perfect k subset K of degree r, B=K+m and A=k+m Noetherian local of equal positive dimension, L_A(q)=r*L_B(q)-(r-1) for every q=p^e, hence e_HK(A)=r*e_HK(B).
claims.falsification_condition: Failure of K-stability of m^[q]_A, the A-module exact sequence, the residue-degree length lemma, or the positive-dimension limit step.

claims.statement: For every r>=1,d>=1,q=2^e in the stated node family, L_A(q)=1+r*((2q-1)q^(d-1)-1), giving e_HK(B)=2 and e_HK(A)=2r. The local pullback is essentially finite type over F2.
claims.falsification_condition: A failed normal-form count, local denominator normalization, finite-generation argument, dimension identification or all-q limit.

claims.statement: Stacks10.52.3,10.52.6,10.52.12 provide length additivity, residue-vector-space length for annihilated modules, and residue-degree-weighted restriction of a finite-length B-module. They do not establish ideal equality for the pullback.
